secret_gate_defect_found_and_closed.what: scripts/qa_secrets.mjs read every file as UTF-8. PowerShell redirection writes UTF-16LE, in which C:/Users/<name>/ is stored with a NUL between every character, so no rule matched and the file reported clean. All thirteen credential rules and the home-path rule were blind to any UTF-16 file.
secret_gate_defect_found_and_closed.what_it_hid: Six tracked pdflatex console captures under docs/dissertation (compile1, compile2, doi_compile1, doi_compile2, final_compile1, final_compile2) each named the local Windows account on 20 distinct paths. The repository is public.
secret_gate_defect_found_and_closed.proof: Same HOME_PATH regex, same file: utf8 decode gives 0 matches, utf16le decode gives 20 matches with account 'lalwa'.
secret_gate_defect_found_and_closed.gate_before: 27/0, 477 of 779 tracked files read against 13 credential rules. Green over a real leak.

secret_gate_defect_found_and_closed.fix: Encoding is now sniffed from the bytes (BOM, else NUL parity). Six self-checks added, including one asserting the old UTF-8-only read would have missed it. .gitignore gained docs/dissertation/*compile*.txt. The six files were removed from the index with git rm --cached and remain on disk.
secret_gate_defect_found_and_closed.sweep: Whole tracked tree re-swept with the gate's own binary filter: 471 non-binary tracked files, 0 UTF-16 text files remaining.
secret_gate_defect_found_and_closed.still_open_and_author_owned: git rm --cached stops republication; it does not remove the files from commits already pushed to the public remote. Rewriting published history is irreversible and is not an agent decision. The disclosed value is a Windows account name, not a credential, so nothing needs rotating.
